spec.title: Read the control on the log line
spec.intro:
A control's continuous evidence is born once, at the source, in a single structured log line — at a
field you can point to. You are handed the real RFC 5424 example lines and asked to read three
control claims directly off the slots: "auth failures are recorded at an alertable Severity"
(the PRI byte), "audit records attribute the actor" (a NILVALUE where a value belongs), and "machine
evidence lives in named fields" (STRUCTURED-DATA) — then trace where evidence is born versus queried,
map each field to the control it evidences, and diagnose the single field where a real downgraded
line breaks its claim.

This surface is the log line itself, rendered as nested named regions (the OSI move applied to a
log). Selecting a region reveals the parser's real decode — including the PRI bit-unpack into its
Facility (PRIVAL / 8) and Severity (PRIVAL mod 8). Every value is the parser's computation over the
real characters; nothing is invented; the line is the answer key. Start on the clean auth-failure
line (ex1-clean).

tasks.instruction:
On the clean auth-failure line (panel "ex1-clean"), select the `HOSTNAME` HEADER slot and read
the value. A log line is a structured record with named slots at fixed positions — this is the
machine that wrote the line.

hints.nudge: The HEADER is space-delimited; HOSTNAME is the slot after TIMESTAMP.

hints.concept: §4.1 — HEADER = PRI VERSION SP TIMESTAMP SP HOSTNAME SP APP-NAME SP PROCID SP MSGID

hints.reveal: Select the HOSTNAME slot; it reads mymachine.example.com

tasks.explain:
A log line is not prose — it is a record with named slots at fixed positions, exactly like the
dock form in §3. You located HOSTNAME by its position in the grammar, not by guessing where the
hostname "looks like" it is. That positional structure is what makes a log line queryable evidence.

tasks.instruction:
Still on ex1-clean, select the `PROCID` slot and read it. This is a NILVALUE `-` — state that it
means the field is genuinely ABSENT (no process id recorded), not the literal text "dash".

hints.nudge: A lone hyphen in a slot is RFC 5424's way of writing "nothing here."

hints.concept: §4.2 — NILVALUE `-` is a real absence; a `-` in an actor field breaks attributability

hints.reveal: Select PROCID; the parser reads it as '- (NILVALUE — absent)', not the text 'dash'

tasks.explain:
The parser reports `-` as a genuine absence, not a string. This matters for control evidence: an
audit record whose actor field is NILVALUE cannot attribute the action, so "privileged actions are
attributable to a user" would be broken by a `-` where a username belongs. Absence is sometimes the
finding.

tasks.instruction:
Select the PRI's `Facility` (panel ex1-clean). The PRI is bit-packed: PRIVAL = Facility×8 + Severity.
Recover the Facility from the high bits (PRIVAL ÷ 8) and read which subsystem spoke.

hints.nudge: The PRIVAL is 34; integer-divide by 8 to get the Facility code, then read its keyword.

hints.concept: §4.3 — Facility = PRIVAL ÷ 8 (the high bits); Facility 4 = security/authorization

tasks.explain:
One small number carried two facts. 34 ÷ 8 = 4 = the security/authorization subsystem — the right
Facility for an auth event. You did the arithmetic the writer did, in reverse. Nothing was looked up
from an answer key; the formula IS the oracle.

tasks.instruction:
Now select the PRI's `Severity` (panel ex1-clean). Recover it from the low three bits (PRIVAL mod 8)
and read the Severity word — this is the slot a "page on Critical-or-worse" alert rule reads.

hints.nudge: 34 mod 8 leaves the remainder that names the Severity word.

hints.concept: §4.4 — Severity = PRIVAL mod 8; it is the field the alert predicate reads

hints.reveal: Select pri.severity; 34 mod 8 = 2 = Critical — an alert on Critical-or-worse fires

tasks.explain:
Severity 2 (Critical) is what makes this auth failure page someone. Severity is not decoration — it
is the control parameter the alert rule evaluates. Hold this value; the broken twin will change only
this one number and silence the alert.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to the structured line (panel "ex3-structured"). Peel the STRUCTURED-DATA element and select
its `SD-ID`. This is the enterprise-namespaced id under which machine-readable control evidence lives.

hints.nudge: The bracketed [ ... ] block is STRUCTURED-DATA; the first token inside is the SD-ID.

hints.concept: §4.5 — SD-ELEMENT = SD-ID + name="value" SD-PARAMs; machine-readable, queryable evidence

hints.reveal: Select the SD-ID inside the brackets; it reads exampleSDID@32473

tasks.explain:
The SD-ID namespaces the element so vendors do not collide. Everything under it is key-value, which is
why a control mapped to a named SD-PARAM is provable by query — unlike the same fact buried in free-text
MSG, which you would have to read by eye.

tasks.instruction:
Still on ex3-structured, select the named `eventID` SD-PARAM and read its value. A query can ask for
events by this name with no English parsing — this is what makes a structured field provable evidence.

hints.nudge: Inside the SD-ELEMENT, the parameters are name="value" pairs; find the one named eventID.

hints.concept: §4.5 — a control mapped to a named SD-PARAM is continuously, automatically verifiable

hints.reveal: Select the eventID SD-PARAM; it reads eventID="1011"

tasks.explain:
`eventID="1011"` is addressable by name. A SIEM rule can ask "every line where eventID is the lockout
code" without parsing prose. That queryability is the whole reason control evidence belongs in
STRUCTURED-DATA rather than in the human MSG slot.

tasks.instruction:
Trace the log pipeline: assemble the five stages in order — source, collector, store, query, alert.
State where evidence is BORN (once, at the event) and where it is QUERIED (repeatedly, afterward).

hints.nudge: Follow one line's life: emitted at the event, shipped, indexed, asked about, then alerted on.

hints.concept: §4.6 — evidence is born at the source (once) and queried at the store (repeatedly)

hints.reveal: Order: source → collector → store → query → alert; born at the source, queried at the store

tasks.explain:
Evidence is born at the source, exactly once, the instant the event happens — everything downstream is
a copy or a question about it. If the source never emitted the line, no query of the store will ever
find it: the gap is upstream of every dashboard. Retention (AU-11) is a property of the store, not the
source.

tasks.instruction:
Map each deciding field onto the control it evidences: the PRI Severity (auth alerting) → AC-7/IA-5,
the audit-record content (actor/time/outcome) → AU-3, the store retention horizon → AU-11. Then
classify the two example lines: the auth-failure line is AUDIT evidence; the do-nuts line is APPLICATION
noise.

hints.nudge: Each control names a field — match the field to the family whose claim that field decides.

hints.concept: §4.7–§4.8 — Severity/outcome → AC-7/IA-5; audit content → AU-3; retention → AU-11

hints.reveal: pri-severity→AC-7/IA-5, audit-content→AU-3, retention→AU-11; auth line=audit, do-nuts=application

tasks.explain:
A control is a predicate over a field. AC-7/IA-5 read the auth outcome and Severity; AU-3 reads whether
the audit content is present and non-NILVALUE; AU-11 reads the store's retention. And not every line is
control evidence — the do-nuts application line lacks the audit content, so offering it as audit proof is
itself a finding, no matter the logging volume.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to the broken twin (panel "pair-auth-severity-broken"). It is the SAME auth failure with only
the PRIVAL changed. Select the PRI `Severity` and read the single field where the real downgraded line
contradicts the "auth failures are alerted" claim.

hints.nudge: Both lines are real and identical but for the PRI — compute the broken line's Severity.

hints.concept: §4.4 — Severity is where a logged-but-silent control failure hides; 39 mod 8 = 7 (Debug)

hints.reveal: On the broken panel, select pri.severity; 39 mod 8 = 7 = Debug — under the Critical alert threshold

tasks.explain:
The discriminating field is the parser's arithmetic over the real PRI byte, not your opinion: 39 = 4×8+7,
so same Facility 4 but Severity 7 (Debug). The event is still logged — a naive "we log auth failures"
check passes — but a Critical-threshold alert never fires on Debug. The break is one number (AC-7/AU-3;
SOC 2 CC7.2/CC7.3), and your Log Evidence Finding names the field, both values, the control, and the ref.

tasks.instruction:
In 4–6 sentences, for a non-technical colleague: explain why a log line is a pre-printed form with
slots and not a paragraph; why the PRI's Severity slot — not the message text — decides whether anyone
is alerted; and why evidence is born once at the source and only queried at the store (so a dashboard
is a question, not the proof). Use the §3 dock-form model, not jargon.

hints.nudge: The §3 model: a clerk's pre-printed form with fixed slots — the priority stamp decides who gets paged.

hints.concept: §3 — The Mental Model + §4.6 born-at-the-source vs queried-at-the-store
